title: Metabolite glues as a means of purine sensing and chemotherapeutic response.
data_url: https://www.rcsb.org/structure/9Q0M (plus PDB 9Q0N, 9Q0O; PRIDE PXD077951; MassIVE MSV000101706)

verified.what_i_actually_checked: Downloaded and parsed PDB entry 9Q0M (2.4 MB mmCIF, 21,868 atom records, 2 protein chains, cryo-EM at 3.1 A, 'PPAT-NUDT5 complex bound to AMP'); confirmed only three structures exist (9Q0M/9Q0N/9Q0O). Read the PRIDE record for PXD077951 via the PRIDE application programming interface: it is FLAG immunoprecipitation mass spectrometry of NUDT5 wild-type, NUDT5 Y74F, and a sequential PPAT-NUDT5 pulldown from one cell line (HEK293T) - a handful of samples, not a measurement table. Counted the compound series named anywhere in the full text: 8 distinct purine/thiopurine analogues (AMP, 6-methylthioinosine monophosphate and its ribonucleoside, 6-ethyl and 6-benzyl versions, 6-methylthioguanosine).
verified.what_came_from_paper_text_only: The CRISPR (clustered regularly interspaced short palindromic repeats) screen size (~3,000 metabolic genes, 8 guides per gene, one cell line, one drug-versus-vehicle comparison analysed with MAGeCK) comes from the methods section only. The per-figure Source Data spreadsheets could not be retrieved: Europe PMC's supplementaryFiles endpoint hit its hard deadline twice and the PubMed Central open-access package returned 404, so I never saw the numerical source tables. The MassIVE metabolomics record MSV000101706 timed out.

a1_downloadable.note: Verified: PDB 9Q0M downloaded and parsed with no login; PRIDE PXD077951 metadata is public. Per-figure Source Data was not retrievable in this session, but nothing is access-controlled.

a2_label_is_a_column.note: No candidate label sits in a downloadable column. Glue potency exists only as plate-reader and gel curves inside per-figure Source Data spreadsheets I could not retrieve; a structure-based label would have to be built from 3 coordinate files.

a3_inputs_present.note: For the only large table (the ~3,000-gene CRISPR screen) the features do not exist at all - you would have to construct gene-level features from outside resources. Not checked in files; screen size read from methods.

a4_units_stated.note: Units are stated in figure legends and methods (nM drug concentrations, angstrom resolution, log fold change for the screen). Verified in the full text, not in the numeric files.

a5_enough_rows.note: Decisive failure, verified: 3 cryo-EM structures and 8 purine/thiopurine analogues named in the whole paper. Against a >=1,500-row bar (>=400 for classification) this is two orders of magnitude short.

a6_fits_laptop.note: Everything here is tiny - the largest file I opened was a 2.4 MB mmCIF. Raw mass spectrometry in PRIDE would be large but is not needed and is excluded by policy.

a7_counts_match_paper.note: The three deposited accessions in the data availability statement match the three live PDB entries; I confirmed 9Q0M resolves to the AMP complex as described.

a8_label_provenance.note: Labels that do exist are physical measurements (cryo-EM density, flow cytometry ratios, plate-reader luminescence), not another model's output. Not the failing killer here.

existing_models.name: GlueMap (molecular dynamics simulation plus a supervised variational autoencoder with attention-based regression, 2025 bioRxiv preprint)
existing_models.score_and_split: Search summary reports it predicts degradation potency from structural features and recovered known degraders plus nine new molecular glues with DC50 (concentration for 50% target degradation) under 50 nM from a 12-billion-compound virtual screen; no split details retrieved.
existing_models.authors_named_unsolved: Not retrieved - I read the search summary, not the paper.

existing_models.name: TriGlue (generative model for molecular-glue-induced ternary complexes, arXiv preprint)
existing_models.score_and_split: Generates the three-body complex in two stages (interface estimation, then interface-conditioned generation); no numbers retrieved beyond the abstract summary.

existing_models.name: MGBench / MG-PDB benchmark of co-folding methods including AlphaFold 3 (J. Chem. Inf. Model. 2025)
existing_models.score_and_split: Curated 221 noncovalent molecular-glue ternary complexes; on 88 structures held out from co-folding training sets, AlphaFold 3 reached 50.6% success on the protein-protein interface and 32.9% on recovering the glue-protein interaction.
existing_models.authors_named_unsolved: Two-thirds of glue-protein contacts are still mispredicted, per the reported success rate.

backbone.name: ESM-2 (protein language model) or a co-folding model such as Boltz/AlphaFold 3 would fit the data type
backbone.hardware: Irrelevant at n=8 labelled compounds; nothing to fit a head on.
backbone.licence: PDB coordinates are public domain (CC0); the paper is CC BY 4.0.

integration.partner_dataset: MG-PDB / MGBench (221 curated molecular-glue ternary complexes) and PDBbind-style ternary sets
integration.join_key: PDB identifier plus UniProt accessions (PPAT = Q06203, NUDT5 = Q9UKK9, both text-mined from the paper)
integration.bigger_question_one_sentence: Do co-folding models that were trained before these structures existed correctly place a nucleotide at a newly discovered glue interface - a 3-structure prospective test, which is a blog post, not a project.

controls.positive_control: Re-predicting the three deposited complexes with a co-folding model and scoring interface recovery against the deposited coordinates.
controls.negative_control: Shuffle which nucleotide is docked into which interface; no meaningful label-shuffling control exists at n=3.
controls.external_validation: MGBench's 88 held-out ternary structures, if one were testing a co-folding model - but that benchmark already exists and was published in 2025.

honest_claim_h3: With three cryo-EM structures and eight compounds, the only honest claim available is 'a published co-folding model does or does not reproduce three newly deposited structures', which is a case report rather than a model.

plain_idea.one_liner: Use a small molecule's shape plus two protein surfaces to predict how strongly it sticks those proteins together.
plain_idea.train_on: What a model would see: a compound structure and the two protein sequences or surfaces it bridges. In this paper that is 8 purine and thiopurine analogues against one protein pair, with 3 experimental structures - a number I verified by downloading the Protein Data Bank entries and counting compound names in the text.
plain_idea.predict: How strongly the compound glues the two proteins (binding strength or complex abundance). The true answer here comes from gel-based pulldowns, mass photometry and plate-reader growth assays reported only inside per-figure source-data spreadsheets that I could not retrieve.
plain_idea.why_worthwhile: Chemists designing molecular glues would like to rank analogues before synthesising them; but this paper supplies 8 analogues against one protein pair, so nothing here can train or honestly test such a model.

more_or_better_data.why: This paper adds 3 ternary structures and 8 compounds; the MG-PDB benchmark already curates 221 molecular-glue ternary complexes, so our contribution is roughly 1% of an existing public set.

confidence_score.why: Replicates exist (n = 3 biological replicates in several assays) but with 8 compounds there is no way to estimate per-prediction uncertainty that would mean anything.

models_beatable.why: The relevant 2025 work (AlphaFold 3 evaluated on 88 structures excluded from its training data, GlueMap, TriGlue) is recent and evaluated on held-out structures; there is no weak old baseline to displace and no data here to displace it with.

guaranteed_improvement.why: Fails the first condition: our training set would be 8 compounds, far less than what any existing model saw, so adding this data cannot make predictions better by construction.

ml_idea: The only tasks the paper could support are (a) predict glue potency of purine-analogue chemotherapeutics at the PPAT-NUDT5 interface, and (b) predict drug-modifier genes from a metabolism-focused CRISPR screen. Task (a) has 8 compounds; task (b) has roughly 3,000 genes from a single screen in a single cell line with no features supplied, and DepMap plus published CRISPR compendia already cover that framing far better.

effort.compute_note: Everything here is trivially small - the 2.4 MB mmCIF I downloaded is the biggest relevant file. Estimated, not timed; compute was never the constraint.
effort.cheapest_killing_check: Count the labelled examples: 3 deposited structures and 8 named compounds. That single count, which takes two minutes, kills the project.

verdict_reason: A mechanistic structural-biology paper, not a dataset. Verified by opening the files: 3 cryo-EM structures and 8 purine analogues, with immunoprecipitation mass spectrometry from one cell line and a single-condition CRISPR screen whose features do not exist. Fails A5 (far under 1,500 rows), A2 (any glue-potency label lives in unretrievable per-figure spreadsheets) and A3. The molecular-glue modelling field already has a 221-complex benchmark, so these three structures are at best three extra test cases for somebody else's model.
